competitors.name: ThermGAS (formerly Thermal Gas Systems)
competitors.industry_focus: Refrigerant and specialty-gas leak monitoring (mechanical rooms, data centers, semiconductor, battery manufacturing)
competitors.us_presence: U.S. headquarters and manufacturer; notable-installations list names organizations across North America (company claim, refrigerant applications).
competitors.battery_experience: Published DMC application note (2026) and battery webpage; no public battery-plant customer reference found.
competitors.rationale: Sponsor. PAIR fixed monitors marketed for DMC vapor monitoring in Li-ion battery manufacturing.

competitors.name: ION Science
competitors.hq: Royston (Fowlmere), UK; U.S. office Stafford, TX
competitors.industry_focus: Photoionization (PID) VOC detection - portable, personal and fixed
competitors.us_presence: ION Science Inc. office (4153 Bluebonnet Dr, Stafford, TX 77477). Official Where-to-Buy page tags U.S. distributors in CT, IL, FL, UT, NJ, GA, TX, CA, LA, MA (company-to-state pairing not machine-readable; to be confirmed).
competitors.battery_experience: FALCO 2 11.7 lists 'Li-ion Battery Manufacturing and Storage' among typical applications; publishes DMC response factors (11.7 eV RF 1.50; 10.6 eV RF 60).
competitors.relationship: Closest direct competitor: fixed DMC-capable VOC monitor explicitly marketed to Li-ion battery manufacturing.
competitors.rationale: Same task (fixed continuous vapor monitoring in battery plants); different technology (PID, non-selective).

competitors.name: Riken Keiki (U.S.: RKI Instruments)
competitors.hq: Tokyo, Japan (Riken Keiki); U.S. subsidiary RKI Instruments, Union City, CA
competitors.industry_focus: Industrial fixed and portable gas detection
competitors.us_presence: RKI Instruments office in Union City, CA (verified on RKI site). PK Safety (CA) is RKI's #1 distributor and factory-authorized service center (verified); AFC International (DeMotte, IN) is a large RKI distributor (Inferred, search excerpt). Full U.S. distributor list not published.
competitors.battery_experience: Official Riken Keiki battery page: electrolyte-filling monitors for DMC/EMC/DEC; >10,000 detectors operating at Li-ion production sites worldwide; 20+ years in Li-ion; case study of a ppm-level range customised for an electrolyte-filling customer. Also NMP duct monitors (SD-2500/2600), testing (GD-70D) and separator (FI-900).
competitors.relationship: Direct competitor with the broadest battery-process portfolio (drying, filling, testing, separator). DMC-specific detection limits not published.
competitors.rationale: Official product page names the same task (electrolyte filling) and the same solvents. RKI (Union City, CA) is the U.S. channel; PK Safety (CA) is an authorized service center.

competitors.name: Honeywell (Li-ion Tamer; RAEGuard 2 PID)
competitors.hq: USA (corporate HQ not re-verified in this session)
competitors.industry_focus: Building automation, fire/life safety, industrial gas detection
competitors.company_size: Not collected (large public company; figures not used in this analysis)
competitors.us_presence: Products sold in U.S. via Honeywell Building Automation and resellers (e.g., Instrumart list price). Li-ion Tamer Gen2+ holds a California State Fire Marshal listing (Jan 2025).
competitors.battery_experience: Li-ion Tamer acquired from Nexceris (July 2025); detects electrolyte solvent vapor off-gas events in battery racks/ESS; UL 2075 recognition for electrolyte solvent vapor (DEC, DMC, EMC) reported. Honeywell markets an integrated "Gigafactory Fire Solution" built around Li-ion Tamer Gen 3 + VESDA for battery production plants (S38, S43). Public U.S. reference: Alamitos Energy Center BESS, Long Beach CA (S39).
competitors.relationship: Event detection (cell venting) rather than DMC concentration monitoring; strong brand and fire-system channel.
competitors.rationale: Different measurement (rate-of-change off-gas event, FM 6540 approved) but competes for the same gigafactory safety budget. Conflict: Gen 3 product page marked Discontinued while the Gen 3 data sheet and gigafactory page remain current - unresolved.

competitors.name: Cubic Sensor and Instrument Co., Ltd.
competitors.hq: Wuhan, China; North American JV 'Cubic Innovaer' (Dec 2025, location not stated)
competitors.industry_focus: Gas sensor modules (NDIR, ultrasonic) and analyzers for OEMs
competitors.company_size: Not collected (listed on Shanghai exchange, ticker 688665)
competitors.us_presence: North American JV Cubic Innovaer announced Dec 2025; no verified U.S. office address or distributor found.
competitors.battery_experience: ATRS-1050 designed for DMC/EMC/EC vapor detection for thermal runaway and battery manufacturing leak detection (catalog).
competitors.relationship: OEM component sensor; DMC-specific NDIR but at high-ppm scale (0-10,000 ppm; +/-200 ppm in 0-2,000 ppm).
competitors.rationale: Detects DMC but resolution suits leak/thermal-runaway events, not low-ppm trace monitoring. Could be integrated by system builders as a low-cost alternative.

competitors.name: NevadaNano (Nevada Nanotech Systems, Inc.)
competitors.industry_focus: MEMS 'Molecular Property Spectrometer' (MPS) gas sensors for flammable gas and refrigerants
relevant_products: MPS Flammable Gas Sensor (H2 + DMC + EMC classification)
competitors.company_size: Not Publicly Available (directory estimates vary 11-100 employees; not used)
competitors.us_presence: U.S. headquarters in Nevada; sells sensors to OEMs.
competitors.battery_experience: Markets DMC/EMC classification for BESS off-gas early warning; no field calibration, 15-year sensor life (vendor claim).
competitors.relationship: Component supplier for BESS/battery-safety devices; adjacent to factory DMC monitoring.
competitors.rationale: DMC-capable but positioned for BESS enclosures; no concentration/LOD spec for DMC published on page read.

competitors.name: Infrasensing
competitors.industry_focus: Environmental monitoring sensors for data centers / critical facilities
competitors.us_presence: Sold 'through OEM partners in select markets'; no U.S. office verified.
competitors.battery_experience: Detects DMC, DEC, EMC off-gas in stationary Li-ion/BESS racks; calibration-free; UL 61010 recognized; explicitly 'not a fire detection or life safety system'.
competitors.relationship: Rack-level BESS/data-center off-gas monitoring; overlaps ThermGAS's data-center audience, not factory DMC.
competitors.rationale: Adjacent customer segment (data centers) where ThermGAS also sells refrigerant monitors.

competitors.name: MSA Safety (incl. Bacharach)
competitors.hq: USA (HQ not re-verified in this session)
competitors.industry_focus: Safety products incl. fixed gas detection; HVAC-R leak detection via Bacharach (acquired July 2021, $337M)
competitors.us_presence: U.S. company with national distribution (details not collected).
competitors.battery_experience: None found for DMC. Chillgard 5000 gas list is refrigerants only.
competitors.relationship: Uses the same PAIR principle (1 ppm refrigerants) - the most credible technology peer if it chose to configure for DMC; main rival in ThermGAS's core refrigerant market.
competitors.rationale: Not a DMC competitor today; strategic threat in core business and potential entrant.

competitors.name: Gasmet Technologies (a Nederman company)
competitors.hq: Vantaa, Finland; North American entity Mississauga, ON, Canada
competitors.industry_focus: FTIR multi-gas analyzers (emissions, process, safety, portable)
relevant_products: GT6000 Mobilis with GAS-LIB-BTRY Li-ion battery library
competitors.us_presence: Sold via U.S. distributors/rental houses (e.g., Advanced Test Equipment Corp., San Diego CA); no U.S. office verified.
competitors.battery_experience: Fixed Li-ion battery library includes DMC, EMC, EC, DEC, HF, CO, H2-related species (dated 2025-11-14).
competitors.relationship: Multi-component FTIR used for battery off-gas / abuse testing; could substitute for area monitoring at higher cost/complexity.
competitors.rationale: DMC capability verified in library; positioned for testing/analysis rather than permanent area alarms.

competitors.name: INFICON
competitors.hq: Bad Ragaz, Switzerland (Inferred); U.S. office East Syracuse, NY
competitors.industry_focus: Leak detection, vacuum and gas analysis instruments
competitors.us_presence: U.S. office in East Syracuse, NY; rental via Advanced Test Equipment Corp. (CA).
competitors.battery_experience: End-of-line leak testing of pouch/prismatic/round/coin cells; quadrupole MS detects electrolyte solvents; 1e-6 mbar.l/s helium-equivalent; 'E-Check (DMC)' accessory listed.
competitors.relationship: Cell-level QC substitute: catches leaking cells before they reach storage/aging areas, reducing the need for ambient alarms; does not monitor room air.
competitors.rationale: Different task (product leak test) but addresses the same root cause (electrolyte leakage).

competitors.name: Advanced Energy (INNOVA / formerly LumaSense)
competitors.relationship: Same physical principle (photoacoustic IR, ppb-level for some gases per search excerpt) but no DMC or battery evidence; official datasheet URL returned 404.
competitors.rationale: Kept as watch-list substitute; not used in comparisons until a current datasheet is obtained.

competitors.battery_experience: None found (SF6, refrigerant, anesthetic, emissions uses).

meta.title: ThermGAS U.S. Competitive Intelligence - Phase 4 analysis
meta.disclaimer: Independent student research by Northeastern University MSBA students. Not an official ThermGAS publication. Vendor specifications are vendor claims unless stated otherwise; no laboratory testing was performed.

headline_findings.title: Two verified direct competitors: ION Science and Riken Keiki/RKI
headline_findings.body: Both officially market fixed detectors for Li-ion battery manufacturing with DMC named as a target: ION Science FALCO 2 11.7 lists 'Li-ion Battery Manufacturing'; Riken Keiki lists DMC/EMC/DEC monitors for electrolyte filling and claims >10,000 detectors at Li-ion plants worldwide.
headline_findings.so_what: These are the vendors a battery-plant EHS buyer will compare ThermGAS against. Neither publishes a DMC detection limit under stated conditions - a published, test-conditioned DMC spec would be a differentiator.

headline_findings.title: The 11.7 eV PID trade-off is documented by the competitor itself
headline_findings.body: FALCO 2 11.7 reads DMC well (RF 1.50) but its lamp lasts up to 4 months (3-month lamp warranty) and a PID responds to every compound below 11.7 eV, so it cannot tell DMC from IPA or ethanol. The 10.6 eV TVOC 2 barely sees DMC (RF 60).
headline_findings.so_what: ThermGAS's strongest evidence-backed angle is selectivity plus maintenance burden - but the cost side must be proven with real lamp and labor quotes.

headline_findings.title: Honeywell sells event detection into the same gigafactory budget
headline_findings.body: Li-ion Tamer Gen 3 detects off-gas venting (10 ppm/s rate threshold, FM 6540) and Honeywell packages it with VESDA as a 'Gigafactory Fire Solution'. It does not report DMC concentration.
headline_findings.so_what: Position ThermGAS as a complement (continuous DMC concentration in filling / electrolyte-handling rooms), not as a rival 'earliest warning' device.

headline_findings.title: ThermGAS's own DMC evidence has gaps
headline_findings.body: Battery webpage says 0.5 ppm; the DMC application note says 1 ppm; DMC is absent from the Master Gas List; no interference data, no hazardous-area rating and no public battery-plant reference were found.
headline_findings.so_what: Fixing the spec sheet is the cheapest, highest-impact action before any sales push.

headline_findings.title: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant DMC reference
headline_findings.body: The only verified U.S. installation reference in this category is a Honeywell Li-ion Tamer BESS site (Long Beach, CA) - not a factory.
headline_findings.so_what: The first credible U.S. reference site is still up for grabs.
headline_findings.status: Verified (absence of evidence after search, not proof of absence)

headline_findings.title: Competitor local presence is thin where battery capacity is concentrated
headline_findings.body: Verified competitor offices/distributors cluster in CA, TX and the Northeast; the largest announced cell capacity sits in KY, NV, MI, OH, TN and GA, where only GA (ION distributor) and OH/IN (inferred) show competitor channel evidence.
headline_findings.so_what: This is 'not verified', not 'no competition' - national vendors can still sell there - but it marks where channel research and early customer development pay off most.

threat_rules.description: Threat level is derived from two evidence-coded dimensions; no market-share or numeric threat index is used because none can be supported.

task_overlap.High: Officially marketed for continuous DMC / electrolyte-solvent monitoring in battery production areas
task_overlap.Medium: Detects DMC or competes for the same battery-plant safety budget, but measures a different thing (event, generic VOC, high-ppm)
task_overlap.Low: Different task (BESS racks, product leak test, lab analysis) or no DMC capability

battery_gtm.High: Official battery-manufacturing marketing AND verified U.S. office/subsidiary or distributor network
battery_gtm.Medium: Battery marketing OR verified U.S. presence, not both

threats.why: Lists Li-ion battery manufacturing; U.S. office (TX) + distributors in 10 states.
Official battery page names electrolyte filling + DMC; U.S. subsidiary RKI (CA) and authorized service (PK Safety).
Event detection, not concentration, but sold as a gigafactory solution with FM/UL credentials.
Fixed PID in same channel, but 10.6 eV gives a weak DMC response; not marketed for batteries.
Generic 10.6 eV fixed PID; no battery marketing found; public price makes it a budget alternative.
DMC-specific NDIR but +/-200 ppm; OEM module; U.S. channel not verified.
Cell leak testing (substitute at the source); battery-marketed; U.S. office NY.
BESS off-gas sensor component; U.S. HQ (NV).
BESS/data-center rack sensor; U.S. presence not verified.
FTIR battery library for off-gas testing; no U.S. office verified.
No DMC today. Separate note: same PAIR principle - High threat in ThermGAS's core refrigerant business.

battlecards.title: ION Science FALCO 2 11.7 eV
battlecards.their_pitch: Fixed 11.7 eV PID that 'sees' high-ionization VOCs incl. DMC; ATEX/IECEx/UL Zone 1; listed for Li-ion battery manufacturing.

where_they_win.text: Low, published entry price: $3,521 reseller list (diffused unit).
Hazardous-area approvals (UL Class I Zone 1, ATEX, IECEx) for installation in classified areas.
Strong DMC response at 11.7 eV (RF 1.50) and 0.1 ppm sensitivity (isobutylene basis).
U.S. office (Stafford, TX) plus distributors tagged in 10 states.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: Selectivity: PAIR targets DMC's IR absorption; a PID sums every compound below 11.7 eV (IPA, ethanol, methanol) - fewer nuisance alarms in mixed-solvent rooms.
where_thermgas_can_win.status: Inferred (from documented principles; no head-to-head test)

where_thermgas_can_win.text: Maintenance: FALCO lamp lifetime up to 4 months (3-month lamp warranty) vs. no UV lamp / no depletable sensor in PAIR; Haloguard pump life typically 5-6 years.
Coverage: one Haloguard IR scans up to 24 sample points (500 ft tubing) vs. one FALCO per point (diffusion).

landmines.text: ThermGAS has no published hazardous-area rating; electrolyte rooms may be classified (DMC flash point ~17 C).
Multi-point scanning means each point is revisited only once per cycle (<1 min per channel) - slower per-point update than a dedicated PID (T90 60 s).
ThermGAS DMC spec is inconsistent (0.5 vs 1 ppm).

discovery_questions: Which other solvents (IPA, ethanol, EMC/DEC, NMP) are present in the room, and how often do you get nuisance VOC alarms?
Who replaces PID lamps today, how often, and what does each visit cost?
Is the monitored area electrically classified, and could an analyzer sit outside it with sample lines?
evidence_gaps: 11.7 eV lamp price and replacement labor
FALCO installed base in U.S. battery plants

battlecards.title: Riken Keiki / RKI Instruments
battlecards.their_pitch: Gas detection for every Li-ion process step (NMP drying, electrolyte filling, testing, separator); >10,000 detectors at Li-ion plants worldwide; 20+ years in the industry.

where_they_win.text: Breadth: one vendor for NMP duct monitors (up to 200 C), filling-area solvent monitors, test-area and O2 monitors.
Battery credibility: claims >10,000 detectors at Li-ion production sites and a ppm-level filling-area case study.
U.S. subsidiary RKI (Union City, CA) and factory-authorized service via PK Safety.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: DMC specificity: Riken's filling monitors are combustible (hot-wire) or NDIR types with no published DMC limit; ThermGAS can publish a DMC-specific ppm spec.
Low-ppm focus: hot-wire combustible sensors are designed for %LEL ranges; low-ppm DMC trend monitoring is a different job.
where_thermgas_can_win.status: Inferred (sensor principle; Riken ppm customisation exists)

where_thermgas_can_win.text: Multi-point extractive sampling from one analyzer.

landmines.text: Riken's case study shows it will customise ranges to ppm for filling customers - do not assume it cannot do low ppm.
Large Asian-OEM battery makers may already standardise on Riken globally.

discovery_questions: Is your gas-detection vendor specified by your global/parent-company standard?
Do you need a %LEL fire-safety alarm, a ppm exposure/leak trend, or both?
What does your current filling-area detector actually read when DMC is present at a few ppm?
evidence_gaps: DMC range/LOD for SD-1RI and SD-D58

battlecards.title: Honeywell Li-ion Tamer Gen 3
battlecards.their_pitch: Earliest off-gas (cell venting) detection, calibration-free, >10-year life, FM 6540 approved; sold with VESDA as a Gigafactory Fire Solution.

where_they_win.text: Brand, fire-system channel and certifications (FM 6540; CSFM listing for Gen2+).
Calibration-free, 10+ year life, bump test with a DEC bottle.
Scales to 100 sensors per controller for rack-level coverage.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: It reports a rate-of-change event, not DMC ppm: no concentration trend for leak hunting, exposure records or process-area alarms.
Designed around battery racks and air streams (monitoring + reference sensors) - a weaker fit for electrolyte-handling or filling rooms.

landmines.text: Bundled into fire-protection projects that ThermGAS may never see; buyer is fire/EHS, budget set early in plant design.
U.S. product page lists Gen 3 as 'Discontinued' while datasheet is current - check before claiming anything about its status.

discovery_questions: Is off-gas event detection already specified by the fire-protection designer?
Who owns electrolyte-leak monitoring in filling/handling rooms - EHS, process or facilities?

battlecards.title: Cubic ATRS-1050 (NDIR module)
battlecards.their_pitch: Low-cost NDIR sensor module for DMC/EMC/EC electrolyte leakage and thermal runaway.

where_they_win.text: DMC-specific optical sensing in a small OEM module with <1 s response (catalog).

where_thermgas_can_win.text: Accuracy at low ppm: ATRS-1050 is +/-200 ppm from 0-2,000 ppm; ThermGAS claims 0.5-1 ppm sensitivity.
Complete monitoring system (alarms, relays, BACnet, multi-point) vs. a component needing integration.

landmines.text: System integrators could build low-cost DMC monitors on Cubic modules; North American JV formed Dec 2025.

discovery_questions: Is your requirement a leak/thermal event alarm or a low-ppm concentration trend?

battlecards.title: MSA Chillgard 5000 (core-market watch)
battlecards.their_pitch: PAIR refrigerant monitor, 1 ppm, 4/8/16 points, BACnet/Modbus, 2-year warranty.

where_they_win.text: Same PAIR principle with published accuracy (+/-1 ppm 0-50 ppm), longer tubing (up to 1,250 ft) and 2-year warranty.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: No DMC on Chillgard's 37-refrigerant gas list - ThermGAS is first PAIR vendor marketing DMC.

landmines.text: MSA could add DMC to a PAIR platform; ThermGAS's technology claim alone is not a moat.

discovery_questions: Do you already run MSA/Bacharach refrigerant monitors on site?
evidence_gaps: Current Chillgard status (UK page shows X30/X50)

battlecards.title: INFICON ELT3000 (substitute at the source)
battlecards.their_pitch: End-of-line mass-spectrometer leak test that finds electrolyte-leaking cells before they leave the line.

where_they_win.text: Catches leaking cells (1e-6 mbar.l/s He-equivalent) before storage/aging; DMC check reference available.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: ELT3000 tests products, not room air - it does not cover spills, fittings, transfer lines or electrolyte storage.

landmines.text: Plants that invest in 100% cell leak testing may see less need for ambient DMC alarms in aging areas.

discovery_questions: Do you leak-test every cell, and where do leaks still reach the room air?

strengths.text: Photoacoustic IR targets DMC's IR absorption; no UV lamp and no depletable electrochemical sensor.
Multi-point extractive design: up to 24 sample points, 3 gases, 500 ft tubing per Haloguard IR.
Integration: relays, 4-20 mA, BACnet interface; UL 3111-1 listed (Haloguard IR).
U.S. manufacturer (Roswell, GA) with decades of refrigerant installations across North America.

weaknesses.text: Conflicting DMC spec (0.5 vs 1 ppm); DMC missing from Master Gas List; no interference data.
No public battery-plant reference or published pricing.
No product-level hazardous-area rating: the Energy page claims Class I Div 1/2 explosion-proof enclosures but names no model or certifier; competitors publish product approvals.
weaknesses.status: Verified (claim found; product rating not found)

weaknesses.text: Scanning multi-point systems update each point less often than dedicated point detectors.

opportunities.text: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant DMC reference.
Capacity ramping in 2025-26: Panasonic KS (since Jul 2025), Toyota NC (Nov 2025), HL-GA GA (H1 2026), LGES AZ (H1 2026).
UBE's Louisiana DMC/EMC plant (100,000 t/y DMC) - a DMC-handling customer outside cell making.
Event detectors (Li-ion Tamer) leave a concentration-monitoring gap ThermGAS can fill as a complement.

threats.text: Honeywell bundles off-gas + smoke detection into gigafactory fire projects.
Riken's large installed base with Asian battery OEMs.
Low entry price of PID point detectors ($3.5k-$3.7k list).
EV-battery slowdown: KORE (AZ) cancelled, Ultium Warren (OH) idle, BlueOval SK split.
MSA's PAIR platform could add DMC.

recommendations.title: Publish one test-conditioned DMC specification
recommendations.action: Resolve 0.5 vs 1 ppm; add DMC to the Master Gas List; publish detection limit, calibration gas, response time per point, and cross-sensitivity to IPA, ethanol, EMC, DEC and NMP.
recommendations.business_case: Neither direct competitor publishes a DMC limit; a credible spec turns ThermGAS's technology claim into a buyer-verifiable advantage.
recommendations.limitation: Requires ThermGAS lab data; results could narrow the advantage if interferents affect PAIR.
recommendations.next_step: Ask the sponsor for DMC calibration and interference test records.

recommendations.title: Position as the DMC-concentration layer that complements event detection
recommendations.action: Message: 'Know how much DMC is in the room, continuously' for electrolyte storage, mixing, transfer and filling rooms - alongside (not instead of) off-gas event systems.
recommendations.business_case: Honeywell owns the 'earliest event warning' story in gigafactories but reports a rate, not ppm; PIDs report ppm but not DMC specifically.
recommendations.limitation: Whether buyers budget for both layers is unverified.
recommendations.next_step: Test the message in 5-8 interviews with battery-plant EHS/process engineers.

recommendations.title: Answer the hazardous-area question before buyers ask
recommendations.action: Document how a remote analyzer with sample lines serves classified rooms, or pursue the relevant approvals.
recommendations.business_case: FALCO 2 11.7 (UL Class I Zone 1) and Riken (explosion-proof) publish approvals; ThermGAS documents do not.
recommendations.limitation: Area classification is site-specific; engineering review needed.
recommendations.next_step: Confirm with ThermGAS engineering which installations are permitted.

recommendations.title: Build the lifecycle-cost case with real quotes
recommendations.action: Collect quotes for FALCO 2 11.7 lamps and service, RKI filling monitors, and ThermGAS configurations for the same room (same number of points).
recommendations.business_case: Point PIDs are cheap to buy ($3,521 list) but need a lamp every ~4 months; one Haloguard IR can cover up to 24 points. The net effect is unknown until priced.
recommendations.limitation: Lamp, labor and ThermGAS prices are Not Publicly Available - no TCO is claimed in this dashboard.
recommendations.next_step: Request three quotations; use the dashboard's scenario fields only with documented inputs.

recommendations.title: Win a first U.S. reference site through a side-by-side pilot
recommendations.action: Offer a 60-90 day pilot in an electrolyte-handling or filling room, logging DMC readings, nuisance alarms and maintenance next to the incumbent detector.
recommendations.business_case: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant DMC reference; a documented pilot becomes the proof every later proposal needs.
recommendations.limitation: Requires plant access and sponsor resources.
recommendations.next_step: Start with priority states below; begin with Georgia (home-state service advantage).

recommendations.title: Build channel coverage where competitors are not verified
recommendations.action: Verify competitor channels in TN, KY, MI, KS and NC, then recruit or equip a local distributor/service partner.
recommendations.business_case: These states hold most operating or ramping cell capacity but show no verified competitor office or distributor in this research.
recommendations.limitation: 'Not verified' is not 'no competition'; national vendors sell everywhere.
recommendations.next_step: Check RKI, Honeywell and ION distributor lists state by state.

state_priority_model.description: Research-prioritisation score, not a market-size or revenue estimate. Only states with at least one verified battery facility are scored; all others show 'Not scored - insufficient evidence'.

inputs.capacity: Announced nominal Li-ion cell capacity (GWh), DOE FCAB (June 2023 data), excluding plants with Verified cancellation
inputs.plants: Number of Li-ion cell plants in the same list
inputs.dmc_plant: 1 if a verified DMC/electrolyte-solvent plant is in the state
inputs.foothold: ThermGAS foothold: 1 = verified HQ state; 0.5 = company-claimed refrigerant reference institutions in the state (Inferred); 0 = none
inputs.competitor_presence: Number of competitors with verified or inferred office/distributor/service/HQ in the state (penalty)
inputs.operating: Plants with a Verified 2025-26 update reporting production start (currently Panasonic De Soto KS and Toyota Liberty NC); targeted/delayed starts are not counted

state_priority_model.formula: score = 100 x [wC*(C/Cmax) + wP*(P/Pmax) + wO*(O/Omax) + wD*D + wF*F - wK*(K/Kmax)] / (wC+wP+wO+wD+wF); negative values shown as 0

meta.title: ThermGAS U.S. Competitive Intelligence - executive layer
meta.status_note: Everything in this file is a research-team PROPOSAL for management consideration. It is not an approved ThermGAS strategy, budget or commitment. Evidence labels: Verified / Inferred / Assumption / Unknown.

core_conclusion.headline: ThermGAS has a credible opening as the DMC-specific, lamp-free concentration monitor that complements event detection, but it cannot yet prove it. Its own DMC specification is inconsistent and no vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant reference.
core_conclusion.next_move: Proposal for management: run a 30-day evidence sprint (fix the DMC spec, answer the hazardous-area question, get real quotes) before committing any pilot hardware or sales spend.

known.text: Two direct competitors sell DMC-capable fixed monitors to battery makers: ION Science FALCO 2 11.7 and Riken Keiki / RKI.
ThermGAS's DMC detection figure conflicts across its own documents (0.5 ppm vs 1 ppm) and DMC is missing from its Master Gas List.
No public U.S. battery-plant DMC customer reference was found for any vendor (absence after search, not proof of absence).
The FALCO 2 11.7 UV lamp lasts up to 4 months (3-month lamp warranty).

inferred.text: PAIR should be more selective for DMC than a PID in mixed-solvent rooms (principle only; no matched test exists).
Honeywell's off-gas event detection is complementary to, not a substitute for, DMC concentration monitoring.
A Georgia-based service model could be an advantage in the Southeast (not tested).

assumed.text: Battery-plant buyers will budget for both an event layer and a concentration layer.
MSA could add DMC to its PAIR-based Chillgard platform.
Large Asian-OEM plants may standardize on Riken globally.

core_conclusion.short: ThermGAS can win as the DMC-specific, lamp-free monitor, but it has to prove its own spec first.
core_conclusion.short_next: Proposal: 30-day evidence sprint before any pilot spend.

key_findings.title: The race is against two named rivals, and neither is unbeatable
key_findings.body: ION Science is cheap to buy ($3,521 list) and hazardous-area approved, but needs a UV lamp roughly every 4 months and cannot tell DMC from other solvents. Riken has the broadest battery portfolio and a claimed 10,000+ detectors in Li-ion plants worldwide, but publishes no DMC detection limit.
key_findings.so_what: A buyer will compare ThermGAS with these two first. ThermGAS wins only with a test-conditioned DMC spec.
key_findings.short: Two direct rivals: ION Science (cheap, lamp change about every 4 months) and Riken (broad, no DMC limit published).

key_findings.title: The U.S. reference-site position is still open
key_findings.body: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant DMC reference. Honeywell sells gigafactory event detection but reports a rate, not DMC concentration.
key_findings.so_what: The first documented plant pilot would be a lasting differentiator, and Honeywell is better treated as a partner-style complement than a head-on rival.
key_findings.short: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant reference yet. The first one is a lasting differentiator.

key_findings.title: ThermGAS's own evidence is the main blocker
key_findings.body: Conflicting DMC spec, no interference data, no product-level hazardous-area rating (the Energy page claims Class I Div 1/2 enclosures without naming a model), no battery reference and no public price. Competitors publish approvals.
key_findings.so_what: These are cheap to fix compared with a sales push, and they decide whether any pilot is credible.
key_findings.short: ThermGAS's own gaps (0.5 vs 1 ppm spec, no product-level hazardous-area rating) are the main blocker.

actions.title: Publish one test-conditioned DMC specification
actions.why: Neither direct competitor publishes a DMC limit; this turns a technology claim into a buyer-checkable advantage.
actions.validation: Spec sheet issued with detection limit, calibration gas, per-point response time and cross-sensitivity to IPA, ethanol, EMC, DEC, NMP; DMC added to the Master Gas List.

actions.title: Answer the hazardous-area question
actions.why: FALCO 2 11.7 (UL Class I Zone 1) and Riken (explosion-proof) publish product approvals. ThermGAS's Energy page claims Class I Div 1/2 explosion-proof enclosures, but no product page names a rating or certifier.
actions.owner_role: Engineering lead with a safety / compliance reviewer
actions.validation: A written position: remote analyzer with sample lines for classified rooms, or a named approval path. Reviewed by qualified engineering.

actions.title: Win a first U.S. reference through a side-by-side pilot
actions.why: A documented pilot becomes the proof every later proposal needs. Start in the home state, where the research found no verified local competitor service.
actions.owner_role: Business Development lead with a Field / Applications engineer
actions.validation: One site signs a pilot protocol covering DMC readings, nuisance alarms and maintenance logged next to the incumbent detector.
actions.status: Proposed - gated on A1 and A2
actions.short: Win a first U.S. reference pilot

decision.question: Should ThermGAS commit to a validation-first U.S. battery pilot program, starting with a 30-day evidence sprint before any pilot hardware or sales spend?

options.label: Do nothing / wait
options.downside: The reference-site opening stays open to ION Science, Riken or Honeywell partners; ThermGAS's spec conflict stays visible to buyers.

options.label: 30-day evidence sprint, then decide on a pilot (research team's proposal)
options.upside: Cheapest way to fix the credibility gaps before spending on a site; keeps a clear Go / No-Go at Day 30.
options.downside: Delays customer contact by about a month; depends on ThermGAS engineering availability.
options.note: Proposal only; not an approved ThermGAS plan.

options.label: Go straight to a pilot
options.downside: A pilot would run on an unresolved spec and an unanswered hazardous-area question, so a weak result or a site-safety objection could cost credibility.

needs_from_management: Release engineering time for the spec and hazardous-area work
Decide whether ThermGAS can supply a pilot analyzer (loan or otherwise)

risks.risk: DMC test shows weaker selectivity or sensitivity than the vendor claim
risks.mitigation: Run the lab test before any customer pilot; reposition on integration and maintenance if needed.

risks.risk: Hazardous-area requirement blocks installation in the target room
risks.impact: Pilot cannot start in the room that matters most.
risks.mitigation: Remote analyzer with sample lines outside the classified area, or a named approval path (action A2).

risks.risk: Honeywell's gigafactory fire bundle fixes the safety budget before ThermGAS is invited
risks.early_warning: Interview feedback on who owns electrolyte-room monitoring
risks.mitigation: Position as the concentration complement; test with 5-8 interviews.

risks.risk: Target plants delay, pause or cancel
risks.early_warning: Plant status re-check at Day 30 and Day 60
risks.mitigation: Prioritize plants with Verified production; keep two candidate sites.

risks.risk: Customer follows a parent-company vendor standard (for example Riken)
risks.mitigation: Prefer U.S. sites with local procurement authority.

risks.impact: The no-lamp technology claim stops being unique.
risks.mitigation: Move first on the published spec and a reference site.

risks.risk: Public-data gaps hide a competitor's real strength (for example Riken DMC range, Honeywell current status)
risks.mitigation: Request datasheets and quotes during the sprint; keep claims labeled.

phases.name: Fix the evidence

items.task: Resolve 0.5 vs 1 ppm; run DMC calibration and interferent tests; publish the spec; add DMC to the Master Gas List
Write the hazardous-area position for classified rooms
Request quotes: FALCO lamp and service, Riken filling monitors; get ThermGAS configuration price
Re-verify status of candidate plants (HL-GA, Queen Creek, SK Commerce, Toyota NC, Panasonic KS) and UBE Louisiana start-up

success: Spec sheet issued with stated test conditions
At least one competitor quote received

gate.name: Go / No-Go #1 (Day 30)
gate.go: Spec and hazardous-area position are complete AND interferent results do not contradict the selectivity claim.
gate.no_go: Lab results contradict the claim, or engineering cannot support the work. Stop and reposition before any customer pilot.

phases.name: Test the message and line up a site

items.task: Complete the interviews; test the 'concentration layer complements event detection' message
items.deliverable: Interview summary: who owns electrolyte-room monitoring, what is budgeted

items.task: Approach Georgia / Southeast plants with verified or planned production for a pilot
items.deliverable: At least two candidate sites and named customer contacts

items.task: Draft the pilot protocol: readings, nuisance alarms, maintenance log, success criteria
Verify competitor channels in TN, KY, MI, KS, NC

success: Interview findings recorded, including who budgets
Customer contact identified at two candidate sites

gate.name: Go / No-Go #2 (Day 60)
gate.go: A site agrees in principle to the protocol AND interviews do not show the message is rejected.
gate.no_go: No site agrees or buyers reject the message. Pivot: revisit the target segment (for example the Louisiana DMC-producer segment) or the positioning.

phases.name: Start the pilot

items.task: Install the analyzer; record a baseline against the customer's existing detector
Weekly log of readings, nuisance alarms and maintenance events
Build the lifecycle-cost comparison from real quotes
Prepare an early readout for management

success: Baseline and first weeks of logs recorded
Comparison built only from documented inputs

gate.name: Go / No-Go #3 (Day 90)
gate.go: Pilot is operating without a safety or access objection AND the log shows usable data. Continue to the full 60-90 day readout.
gate.no_go: Site withdraws, a safety objection is raised, or data is unusable. Stop spending; document lessons.

roadmap.note_after_90: A 60-90 day pilot started inside this plan would finish after Day 90. The full readout and any commercial decision fall outside this 90-day window.

adjacent_opportunity.title: Adjacent opportunity: data center cooling
adjacent_opportunity.short: Data centers are where ThermGAS's core refrigerant business already plays, and Georgia, its home state, has battery plants and one of the largest data center loads.

points.text: ThermGAS already markets refrigerant detection for data center chillers and precision cooling, and flags battery / UPS gas hazards.
MSA / Bacharach (incl. the PAIR-based Chillgard 5000) is actively targeting the same data center buyers.
Data center electricity load is used as a proxy for cooling demand by state. It is not a count of sites or a market size.
States with both a battery opportunity and a large data center load could share one sales and service effort.

dataCenters.description: Data center electricity load by state, 2023 (EPRI Table A1). Used as a proxy for where data center cooling (and therefore refrigerant monitoring demand) is concentrated. It is not a count of facilities, not a market size and not a ThermGAS sales estimate. States not in the table are shown as Not Verified / Insufficient Evidence.

relevance.text: ThermGAS markets refrigerant detection for data center chillers, precision cooling and DX equipment, and flags battery / UPS gas hazards.
MSA / Bacharach actively market refrigerant leak detection (incl. the PAIR-based Chillgard 5000) to data centers.
Infrasensing and Honeywell Li-ion Tamer address battery off-gas in data center / BESS settings.
Data center electricity load is a reasonable proxy for cooling (and refrigerant) intensity by state.

observations.text: The PAIR line (TracePoint 1000, Haloguard IR / III) is what the battery and data center stories rest on; CMOS and oxygen products are a separate, lower-cost refrigerant-safety line.
The Energy page claims explosion-proof enclosures certified for Class I, Div 1 and Div 2, but names no model, certifier or certificate, and no product page lists a hazardous-area rating.
Specs conflict inside ThermGAS pages: Haloguard III says 1 ppm in its header and 20 ppm in its spec table; the battery page and TracePoint say 0.5 ppm while Haloguard IR says 1 ppm.
Only TracePoint 1000 names data centers on its own product page; the Data Centers industry page names no model.
No product page publishes a price.
